snap.desc: Use cones or tires to create a gate for each player. All players carry a puck. On the signal, players must skate through the gate opposite them, avoiding the other players. Fastest through the gate wins. Change to skating through the opposite gate and then back through the original gate.

Players skate around tires working on cross-over skating technique. Keep the stick to the inside. Work both to the left and to the right. Coaches should work individually with players who need technical instruction. Change to forward-to-backward pivots.

Start with one more cone than the number of players, and one IT player in the middle. On the coach's signal, all players must change cones, with no two players ending up at the same cone. The IT player tries to get to a vacated cone before someone else. Outside players must all start and stop facing the middle.

Divide into groups of 2 or 3. Have players skate continuously. Forward to backward, drop to knees, Superman dive, log roll, step over stick, pass stick between the legs, and so on. Change movements on the fly.

Play starts as a 1v1. When the defender steals the puck, they must pass to their waiting teammate, who becomes the new offensive player. The original offensive player becomes the new defender and the original defender exits the play.

Have players pair up, each with a puck. Designate which player is the truck and which is the trailer to start. On the signal to start, the trucks try to shake their trailer and the trailer attempts to stay directly behind and as close as possible to their truck. After 30 to 40 seconds, switch trucks and trailers. Dogfight: have the trailer try to touch the truck's skate with their puck. When touched by the puck, players switch roles.

Players are split into two teams. Each team must push the tires across the ice and touch the tire to the boards on the opponent's side to score a point. Have multiple tires in play. When a goal is scored, the coach drops the tire back at center ice.

Each player starts with a dark and a light hockey sock hanging out of their pants. Divide the group into two teams. On the signal to start, players try to steal their opponents' colored sock while protecting their own. If a player has both socks stolen, they sit out until the round is completed. Repeat for the remaining time.

Players play 1v1 keep-away in the zone. On the whistle to rest, players make stationary passes to each other. Pass cross-body and sweep the puck. Forehand, backhand, and bullet pass as hard as possible. Players must perform a fake before each pass.

Split the players into two groups with all players possessing a puck. One group starts inside the circle, the other outside. On the coach's signal, the inside group tries to speed up their stickhandling to avoid the other players. The outside group skates at a comfortable speed clockwise around the outside of the circle. Switch inside and outside groups every 30 seconds. Switch to counterclockwise after a few reps.
Each team tries to score on the opponent's net. The puck cannot be carried over the red line — it must be passed to a teammate. Play 3v3, or use the whole group with multiple pucks.

Start the game with one less ring than the number of players. On the signal to start, the players attempt to grab a ring with their overturned stick and keep possession until the coaches signal to stop. After each stoppage, remove a ring from the game.
The coach spots a puck into the corner. Two players compete for puck possession. The player who gains the puck attacks the net to score and the other player defends.

Split into groups of 2 to 3 players at each pad, based on the mobility level of the players. This keeps everyone moving. Start with forward-to-backward pivots and backward-to-forward pivots at each end. Change to forward crossovers and backward crossovers. Make sure to go both ways. Pull aside any players who need additional instruction.
Pass the puck off the tire to score. The coach can have 1v1s or 2v2s happening at the same time.
Play 2v2 in a tight space with 40 to 60 second shifts.
Divide players into groups of three. Two players attempt to play keep-away from the other player in their group. If the puck is stolen, a new player becomes the odd man out.

Use the center red line as the pivot point. Players can only skate forward on one side of the line and backward on the other. A coach or designated tagger must try to tag all players. If tagged, the player is frozen until a teammate skates a circle around them and sets them free.

The first player starts with a puck and must go behind the vacant net before attacking the goaltender. The defensive player will angle the offensive player when coming out from behind the vacant net to defend. The offensive player does not have to stop behind the net — let them play out the different situations on their own.

Players pair up starting on each side of a divider pad, one with a puck and one without. The player without the puck attempts to steal their partner's puck without stepping over the barrier. On change of possession, switch roles and start over.
Relay race. Divide players into 2 teams. Lay sticks on the ice in the suggested pattern and have each player work through them and back before the next one goes.

All players have a blue puck. Divide the players into 2 teams. Each team must stay on their designated half of the ice. For 30 seconds players shoot blue pucks to the other team's side of the ice. Team with the least number of pucks on their side when time runs out wins. Repeat several times. Coaching point: emphasize sweeping the puck.

Players stickhandle while skating around obstacles. All players are involved. Check to see that each player is holding their stick properly: hands about shoulder width apart, top hand at the end of the stick partially held in the palm with the V between thumb and forefinger on top of the stick like you would hold a hammer. Use ringette rings instead of pucks.

Give players plenty of pucks and have them spread out around the outside of the face-off circle. Players try to pass or shoot the puck to hit and move the bucket, ball, ring, or whatever object is used. The objective is to move the object outside the circle. Position players perpendicular to the bucket so that they shift weight and sweep the puck.
Two players are designated as the sharks to start. The minnows must skate from blue line to blue line without being tagged. If they are tagged, they become sharks too.
Two on two in your own area. Tires or cones work as goal markers if there are not enough mini nets.
Skate through the nets, weave the tires on an inside edge, then dive under a stick laid across two cones and finish with a shot on net. The next player goes when the one ahead reaches the first tire.

Two teams. Fill the inside of the box with tennis balls or anything light. On the signal a player skates in through the opening, grabs one ball, skates back out and drops it in their tire. Most balls in the tire wins. For a tougher version close the openings so they have to get over the barrier.

Players skate around the tires. On the signal everyone tries to sit in one. Whoever misses out is done. Pull a tire and run it again until one player is left. Keep several games going at once so nobody is standing around.

Work through a series on the whistle: two-foot glide, two-foot glide with butt to heels, running on skates, glide into a two-foot jump, down to both knees and back up, then down to a single knee and up alternating sides.
Coaches throw balls at the group while the players try to dodge out of the way. Anyone who gets hit drops to their knees and gets back up three times before rejoining.
Two on two in a tight area, thirty-second shifts.

Mark the area into three bands. Players in the two outer bands pass to each other through the middle while the middle players try to pick the passes off. Passes must be flat on the ice and direct, not banked off the boards. Anyone in the middle who intercepts swaps places with the passer. Keep three or four pucks going.
Everyone skates backward with their hands on their knees and tries to bump the others off balance. A player is out if they go down or take their hands off their knees. Last one standing wins.

Split the group into threes, one puck per group, each group working in a small area. All three compete for the same puck. Push players to protect and handle the puck rather than simply outskating each other.

Players start in the corner and go one at a time: power turns around three cones, jump the blue line, skate backward to the cone, skate forward and jump the blue line again, then slide on their belly under the stick. Players then grab a puck, skate around the center cone, and shoot on net, aiming for the cone target. Send the next player when the one ahead finishes the second power turn. Time the team and challenge them to beat their time on a second run.

Set up players in two lines at the top of the zone. When coach says go, two players race around three cones (players choose whichever three they want and whatever direction they want), coach spots a puck in the middle and the players battle 1v1 for a shot on net.

Players pair up starting on each side of a divider pad. One player is designated “IT” and tries to tag their partner. Once tagged, switch roles and repeat. Players are not allowed to step over the pads.

Players should spread out. The coach uses his/her stick to direct the players' movements. The players should keep their heads up while staying square to the coach. Start without pucks and add them when the players show basic competency related to the desired skills. The coach can add additional elements such as tapping the stick on the ice to direct the players to drop to their knees and pop up as quickly as possible.

Players start in the corner and go one at a time: power turns around three cones, jump the blue line, skate backward to the cone, skate forward and jump the blue line again, then slide on their belly under the stick. Players then grab a puck, skate around the center cone, and shoot on net, aiming for the cone target. Send the next player when the one ahead finishes the second power turn. Time the team and challenge them to beat their time on a second run.

Players line up in the corner with pucks. Two coaches stand evenly spaced about 10 feet off the boards. Each player passes to the first coach and starts skating, receives a pass back, continues skating, and immediately passes to the second coach. After receiving the return pass from coach 2, players skate out and around the cones, back toward the net, and shoot at the cone placed in the net.

Form two lines at the blue line. The first pair skates up the ice passing back and forth, then shoots at the net once they reach the cone. The next pair starts when the first pair reaches the top of the circle. After shooting, players skate hard back to the end of the opposite line, so they alternate sides and work on both forehand and backhand passes.

Players space out evenly around the circle. Start with one puck and pass it around the circle, working on pivoting with the puck and making forehand passes. Add an extra puck (up to 4) after each full trip “around the world”. Variation: Players pass across the circle, calling the receiver's name first. Coaches help players pick their target as needed.
Players spread around the circle. They must skate up to the cone and stop, attempting to cover the cone with snow. Have players alternate lead foot for stopping.

Place pucks in the center of the circle. Have players in 2 or 3 lines on the outside of the circle. On the whistle one player at a time skates in and takes one puck and skates it to their safe zone. Team with the most pucks wins. Variation: players can steal pucks from the other team. Variation: Split into two teams and have players line up like Gunners Alley. Place all pucks in the middle. Same rules apply.
Divide players into 2 Teams. Teams compete to pass pucks move the target across their opponent's line.
Players skate forward to the first cone, pivot, backwards to the second cone, pivot and race for the puck and shoot on net aiming for the cones in the net.

drills.name: Pre Game Warm Up: Follow the Pass

snap.desc:
1. Position one player at each side of the top of the circle. The remaining players line up in the corner with pucks.
2. The first player passes to the left-side player and follows the pass.
3. The receiver passes across the top of the circle to the right-side player and follows the pass.
4. The right-side player skates in and shoots on net.
Have players make three laps through the peanut skating pattern using both crossovers and tight turns. Have players skate both to the right and to the left, then switch to skating backward.
